subject: maths
title: Year 6 Adding and Subtracting Fractions
seo_title: Year 6 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets: Free Maths with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions using knowledge of equivalent fractions
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on adding and subtracting fractions, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6N05): related and unrelated denominators, fraction bars, number lines, simplest form, mixed numerals with regrouping and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Different denominators? Rename both fractions with a common denominator, then add or subtract the numerators.
key_sub: 1/3 + 1/4 = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12, not 2/7. Write answers in simplest form, and regroup 1 whole when the first fraction in a mixed numeral subtraction is smaller.
body_html:
Make the parts the same size

You can only add or subtract parts that are the same size. Thirds and quarters are different sizes, so first find a common denominator: a number that both denominators divide into. Then write each fraction as an equivalent fraction with that denominator.

Example

13 + 14 = ?

Common denominator: 12. 13 = 412 and 14 = 312. Add the numerators: 4 + 3 = 7.

Answer: 712

On a number line split into twelfths, start at 13 (4 steps) and jump forward 14 (3 steps). You land on 712.

Find the common denominator

If one denominator is a multiple of the other, use the bigger one. Otherwise, find the lowest common multiple of the two denominators. Multiplying the denominators always works too, but the numbers get bigger.

FractionsCommon denominatorEquivalent fractions
12 and 38848 and 38
23 and 1412812 and 312
56 and 34121012 and 912

Simplest form and mixed numerals

Give answers in simplest form: divide the numerator and denominator by their highest common factor. If the answer is an improper fraction, write it as a mixed numeral.

Example

56 + 34 = ?

1012 + 912 = 1912. 19 ÷ 12 = 1 remainder 7, so 1912 = 1 712.

Answer: 1 712

Example

56 − 12 = ?

56 − 36 = 26. Divide the numerator and denominator by 2: 26 = 13.

Answer: 13

Mixed numerals

Write the fraction parts with a common denominator. Then add or subtract the fractions and the whole numbers.

CalculationEquivalent fractionsFractionsWhole numbersAnswer
2 13 + 1 142 412 + 1 3127122 + 1 = 33 712
2 23 + 1 342 812 + 1 9121712 = 1 5122 + 1 + 1 = 44 512
3 14 − 1 233 312 − 1 812regroup: 2 15122 − 1 = 11 712

In the last row, 312 is less than 812, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1212. 3 312 = 2 1512.

Example

3 14 − 1 23 = ?

3 312 − 1 812. Regroup: 3 312 = 2 1512. Fractions: 1512 − 812 = 712. Whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1.

Answer: 1 712

Another way: change both to improper fractions. 3 14 = 3912 and 1 23 = 2012. 3912 − 2012 = 1912 = 1 712.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
13 + 14 = 27 (adding the numerators and the denominators)Use a common denominator: 412 + 312 = 712
12 + 38 = 48 (changing the denominator but not the numerator)Multiply the numerator by the same number: 12 = 48, so the total is 78
3 14 − 1 23 = 2 512 (taking 312 from 812)Regroup 1 whole: 2 1512 − 1 812 = 1 712
56 − 12 = 26 (forgetting to simplify)Divide the numerator and denominator by 2: 13

faq.q: What does AC9M6N05 mean in Year 6 maths?
faq.a: It is the Australian Curriculum v9.0 content description for Year 6 fractions: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions using knowledge of equivalent fractions. Unlike Year 5, the denominators do not have to be related, so 1/3 + 1/4 is included.

faq.q: How do you add fractions with different denominators?
faq.a: Find a common denominator, write both fractions as equivalent fractions with it, then add the numerators. For 1/3 + 1/4, use twelfths: 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12.

faq.q: How do you subtract mixed numerals when the first fraction is smaller?
faq.a: Regroup by renaming 1 whole as a fraction. For 3 1/4 − 1 2/3, write 3 3/12 − 1 8/12, rename to get 2 15/12 − 1 8/12, and the answer is 1 7/12.
No. NAPLAN is for Years 3, 5, 7 and 9. Adding and subtracting fractions in Year 6 builds the skills students need for Year 7 maths and the Year 7 NAPLAN numeracy test.

sets.title: One denominator is a multiple of the other

items.q:
The bar is split into eighths. Green shows 12 and yellow shows 38. What is 12 + 38?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 2, so use 8 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 12 = 48. Add the numerators: 48 + 38 = 78. The answer is 78.

items.q:
The bar is split into sixths. Green shows 13 and yellow shows 16. What is 13 + 16?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 6 is a multiple of 3, so use 6 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 13 = 26. Add the numerators: 26 + 16 = 36. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 36 by 3 to get 12. The answer is 12.

items.q:
The bar is split into eighths. The shaded part is 34, and 38 of the bar is crossed out. What is 34 − 38?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 34 = 68. Subtract the numerators: 68 − 38 = 38. The answer is 38.

items.q:

items.q: To work out 34 + 18, you change 34 into eighths. Which fraction is equal to 34?
items.e: 4 × 2 = 8, so multiply the numerator by 2 too: 3 × 2 = 6. 34 = 68. Then 68 + 18 = 78.

items.q: To work out 23 + 112, you change 23 into twelfths. Which fraction is equal to 23?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. 23 = 812. Then 812 + 112 = 912.

items.q: What is the lowest common denominator of 23 and 34?
items.e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12. The first number in both lists is 12.

items.q: What is the lowest common denominator of 14 and 16?

items.q: What is the lowest common denominator of 38 and 56?
items.e: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24. The first number in both lists is 24. 8 × 6 = 48 also works, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: The green part is 23 and the yellow part is 14. The dashed lines split both bars into twelfths. Which shows both fractions in twelfths?
c: 212 and 112
1112 and 912
812 and 312
612 and 412
items.e: Count the small parts in each shaded piece. 3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator and denominator of 23 by 4: 812. 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the numerator and denominator of 14 by 3: 312. The answer is 812 and 312.

items.q: The green part is 12 and the yellow part is 25. The dashed lines split both bars into tenths. Which shows both fractions in tenths?
c: 110 and 210
210 and 1010
510 and 410
910 and 710
items.e: Count the small parts in each shaded piece. 2 × 5 = 10, so multiply the numerator and denominator of 12 by 5: 510. 5 × 2 = 10, so multiply the numerator and denominator of 25 by 2: 410. The answer is 510 and 410.

items.q: Harper wrote 12 + 13 = 25. What mistake did she make?
c: She added the numerators and the denominators
items.e: Halves and thirds are different sizes, so you cannot add the numerators and the denominators. Use sixths: 36 + 26 = 56. Also, 25 is less than 12, so it cannot be the total.

sets.title: Answers greater than 1 and simplest form

items.q: Write 1712 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 17 ÷ 12 = 1 remainder 5. So 1712 is 1 whole and 512 left over: 1 512.

items.q: Write 229 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 22 ÷ 9 = 2 remainder 4. So 229 is 2 wholes and 49 left over: 2 49.

items.q: Which fraction is already in simplest form?
items.e: A fraction is in simplest form when the numerator and denominator have no common factor except 1. 410 = 25, 69 = 23 and 515 = 13 can all be simplified. 7 and 12 have no common factor, so 712 is in simplest form.

items.q: Zara works out 56 − 13 = 36. What should she write as the final answer?
items.e: 36 is correct, but it is not in simplest form. 3 is a factor of 3 and 6, so divide both by 3: 36 = 12.

Give your answer as a mixed numeral in simplest form.

Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 6 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 5 16 = 5 212 and 2 34 = 2 912. 212 is less than 912, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1212. 5 212 = 4 1412. Subtract the fractions: 1412 − 912 = 512. Subtract the whole numbers: 4 − 2 = 2. The answer is 2 512.

items.q:
6 25 − 3 12 = ?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 5 and 2 is 10, so use 10 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 6 25 = 6 410 and 3 12 = 3 510. 410 is less than 510, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1010. 6 410 = 5 1410. Subtract the fractions: 1410 − 510 = 910. Subtract the whole numbers: 5 − 3 = 2. The answer is 2 910.

items.q:
7 18 − 4 34 = ?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 4 34 = 4 68. 18 is less than 68, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 88. 7 18 = 6 98. Subtract the fractions: 98 − 68 = 38. Subtract the whole numbers: 6 − 4 = 2. The answer is 2 38.

items.q:
Ruby is making pancakes. The recipe uses 34 cup of milk and 13 cup of water. How much liquid is that altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 34 = 912 and 13 = 412. Add the numerators: 912 + 412 = 1312. 1312 is an improper fraction: 1312 = 1 112. The answer is 1 112 cups.

items.q:
A 2 L bottle of water is full. At the athletics carnival, Noah drinks 34 L and Oliver drinks 23 L. How much water is left in the bottle?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: First add what they drink. Use twelfths: 912 + 812 = 1712 = 1 512 L. Then 2 − 1 512: rename 1 whole, 2 = 1 1212. 1 1212 − 1 512 = 712 L.

items.q:
Matilda spends 23 of an hour on maths homework and 14 of an hour reading. How long does she spend altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
c: 1112 of an hour
14 of an hour
34 of an hour
37 of an hour
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 23 = 812 and 14 = 312. Add the numerators: 812 + 312 = 1112. The answer is 1112 of an hour. (That is 55 minutes.)

items.q:
Isla plans to spend 1 14 hours on homework this week. She has done 23 of an hour so far. How much time is left?
Give your answer in simplest form.
c: 712 of an hour
512 of an hour
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 14 = 1 312 and 23 = 812. 312 is less than 812, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1212. 1 312 = 1512. Subtract the fractions: 1512 − 812 = 712. The answer is 712 of an hour. (That is 35 minutes.)

items.q:
Amelia has 3 13 m of ribbon. She uses 1 34 m to wrap a present. How much ribbon is left?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 3 13 = 3 412 and 1 34 = 1 912. 412 is less than 912, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1212. 3 412 = 2 1612. Subtract the fractions: 1612 − 912 = 712. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 712 m.

items.q:
In the school garden, 13 of the ground is for vegetables and 25 is for native plants. The rest is for flowers. What fraction of the garden is for flowers?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: First add the parts that are used. Use fifteenths: 13 = 515 and 25 = 615, so 515 + 615 = 1115. The whole garden is 1515. Flowers: 1515 − 1115 = 415.

items.q:
Lachlan eats 14 of a pizza and Liam eats 13 of it. What fraction of the pizza is left?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: First add what they eat. Use twelfths: 312 + 412 = 712. The whole pizza is 1212. Left: 1212 − 712 = 512.

items.q:
On school camp, a Year 6 class walks 2 14 km to a lookout and then 1 23 km to the campsite. How far do they walk altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 2 14 = 2 312 and 1 23 = 1 812. Add the fractions: 312 + 812 = 1112. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. The answer is 3 1112 km.

items.q:
At cross-country training, Charlotte runs 1 34 km. Aarav runs 1 56 km. How much further does Aarav run than Charlotte?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: “How much further” means subtract. The lowest common multiple of 6 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 56 = 1 1012 and 1 34 = 1 912. Subtract the fractions: 1012 − 912 = 112. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 112 km.

items.q:
A bucket holds 4 15 L of water. Chloe uses 1 23 L to water the vegie patch. How much water is left in the bucket?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 5 and 3 is 15, so use 15 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 4 15 = 4 315 and 1 23 = 1 1015. 315 is less than 1015, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1515. 4 315 = 3 1815. Subtract the fractions: 1815 − 1015 = 815. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 2 815 L.

items.q:
A damper recipe needs 34 kg of flour. Ethan has two bags with 12 kg and 18 kg in them. How much more flour does he need?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: He has 12 + 18 = 48 + 18 = 58 kg. He needs 34 = 68 kg. 68 − 58 = 18 kg more.

items.q:
An Anzac biscuit recipe uses 1 14 cups of rolled oats and 56 cup of flour. How many cups is that altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 14 = 1 312 and 56 = 1012. Add the fractions: 312 + 1012 = 1312. The whole number is 1. 1312 is an improper fraction: 1312 = 1 112. 1 + 1 112 = 2 112. The answer is 2 112 cups.

items.q:
The swimming carnival lasts 4 12 hours. Lunch takes 34 of an hour. How long is left for races?
Give your answer in simplest form.
c: 34 of an hour
items.e: 4 is a multiple of 2, so use 4 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 4 12 = 4 24. 24 is less than 34, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 44. 4 24 = 3 64. Subtract the fractions: 64 − 34 = 34. The whole number left is 3. The answer is 3 34 hours. (That is 3 hours 45 minutes.)

items.q:
A jug holds 1 12 L of orange juice. Kai pours 58 L into glasses. How much juice is left in the jug?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 2, so use 8 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 1 12 = 1 48. 48 is less than 58, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 88. 1 48 = 128. Subtract the fractions: 128 − 58 = 78. The answer is 78 L.

items.q:
Two pieces of timber, 2 23 m and 1 45 m long, are joined end to end to edge a garden bed. What is the total length?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 5 is 15, so use 15 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 2 23 = 2 1015 and 1 45 = 1 1215. Add the fractions: 1015 + 1215 = 2215. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. 2215 is an improper fraction: 2215 = 1 715. 3 + 1 715 = 4 715. The answer is 4 715 m.

items.q:
In a Year 6 class, 12 of the students walk to school and 13 come by car. The rest ride a bike. What fraction of the class rides a bike?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: Add the two groups. Use sixths: 36 + 26 = 56. The whole class is 66. Bike riders: 66 − 56 = 16.

items.q:
William’s bike ride to the beach is 1 16 km. He has ridden 34 km so far. How far is left to ride?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: Work out 1 16 − 34. Use twelfths: 1 16 = 1412 and 34 = 912. 1412 − 912 = 512 km. Check: 912 + 512 = 1412 = 1 16.

items.q:
For the school sausage sizzle, 1 34 kg of onions are cut up in the morning and 2 13 kg at lunch. How many kilograms of onions is that altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 34 = 1 912 and 2 13 = 2 412. Add the fractions: 912 + 412 = 1312.
